title: PingTool - Unsanitized Command Injection (Easy)
description: Execute arbitrary system commands via unsanitized host parameter in the Ping diagnostic utility to read /app/flags/flag_rce.txt.
hints: The ping utility invokes the system ping binary using a shell without sanitizing the target host.
Use standard command chaining operators such as ';' to execute additional shell commands.

title: PingTool - Filter-Bypass Command Injection (Medium)
description: Bypass character blacklists (;, &&, |) in the ping utility to execute system commands and read the medium flag.
hints: Common command delimiters like ';', '&&', and '|' are blocked by a keyword filter.
Notice that newlines (%0a or \n), backticks (`...`), and command substitution $(...) can execute commands without blacklisted characters.

title: PingTool - Whitespace/Binary Bypass Command Injection (Hard)
description: Bypass strict whitespace and command binary blacklists (blocking spaces, ;, &, |, cat, sh, bash) to read the hard flag.
hints: Whitespace and common binaries (cat, sh, bash) are filtered out.
Use internal shell whitespace variables like $IFS or ${IFS}, and substitute 'cat' with tools like 'head', 'tail', 'nl', or input redirection '<'.

title: PingTool - Unrestricted SSRF (Easy)
description: Use the HTTP Health / URL preview tool to reach the internal status endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8005/internal/status and extract the easy SSRF flag.
hints: The preview tool performs HTTP requests directly from the web application server.
Accessing http://127.0.0.1:8005/internal/status from the server bypasses external loopback restrictions.

title: PingTool - SSRF Localhost Filter Bypass (Medium)
description: Bypass a naive string filter that blocks 'localhost' and '127.0.0.1' to retrieve the internal status endpoint flag.
hints: The application only checks whether the literal strings 'localhost' or '127.0.0.1' are present in the URL.
Linux resolves alternate IP notations like 0.0.0.0, 127.1, decimal (2130706433), hex (0x7f000001), or IPv6 [::] to the loopback interface.

title: PingTool - SSRF CIDR/Hex/Redirect Bypass (Hard)
description: Bypass hostname resolution and flawed CIDR validation by exploiting alternative loopback addresses (127.0.0.2) or HTTP redirects.
hints: The resolver checks if the destination matches a restrictive CIDR rule (127.0.0.1/32).
On Linux, the entire 127.0.0.0/8 subnet routes to localhost (e.g., http://127.0.0.2:8005/internal/status), or use an HTTP 302 redirect via /api/redirect.

title: PingTool - Reflected XSS (Easy)
description: Inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript into the diagnostic lookup error response to capture the admin session context.
hints: User input provided in diagnostic host queries is echoed directly into HTML error banners with Jinja's safe filter.
Inject a classic <script>alert(1)</script> payload or check /api/audit/logs to observe reflection and leak the admin token.

title: PingTool - Context-Breaking Reflected XSS (Hard)
description: Break out of an inline JavaScript string context where angle brackets are sanitized to execute arbitrary JavaScript.
hints: The application sanitizes '<' and '>', preventing injection of new HTML tags, but reflects user input inside an inline <script> variable.
Break out of the string boundary using "; alert(1); // without requiring angle brackets.
